description: Record that a design element SATISFIES an EnvironmentRule (COMPLIES_WITH). Pass `verified: true` ONLY when compliance was demonstrated — a calc package, a stamped drawing, a test report — and put what demonstrates it in `evidence`. It defaults to false because a claim is not a check, and the two must stay distinguishable to anyone reading the record later. Ask for this when you want to record that a part meets a regulation or rule the environment imposes. MANY AT ONCE: `draw_edges`, items {"tool": "complies_with", "arguments": {…}}, same checks, all or nothing.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

element_id.description:
The design element that complies. Its type is resolved from the id.
The complying node; its type is `element_type`.

element_type.description: Optional; resolved from the id when omitted.

evidence.description: What demonstrates it — a calc package, a stamped drawing, a test report.

rule_id.description:
The `EnvironmentRule` complied with.
🛑 NOT a `DesignRule` — see `violates_rule.rule_id`.

verified.description:
Whether compliance was DEMONSTRATED rather than merely asserted.
Defaults to false, for the reason every evidence field here does: a
claim is not a check.

name: complies_with
